name: FakeLightInfluenceMode
src_typeComment: A stand-in for a real Light where a full Light component's cost isn't wanted — Built-in RP has no cheap built-in "fake point light" of its own. Two independent, combinable behaviours (as scoped: "explore light influence" alongside the sprite, not instead of it): - Sprite: a camera-facing glow quad at this position, so the LIGHT SOURCE ITSELF reads as lit (a torch flame, a magic orb) without a real Light casting anything. - Influence: tints nearby real renderers' ALBEDO (not emission — see note below) toward this light's colour, falling off with distance, so SURROUNDING geometry also reads as lit. This is the part the sprite alone can't do.  Why albedo (_Color) and not _EmissionColor for influence: emission only renders if the target material already has the _EMISSION keyword + non-black GI flags enabled, which most materials don't by default — that would make the effect SILENTLY do nothing on an unprepared material, exactly the class of bug this toolkit's self-tests exist to catch. Tinting _Color works on any Standard-shader material with zero setup.  KNOWN LIMITATION, accepted rather than solved: if two FakeLights' influence radii overlap the same renderer, whichever rescans last wins — there's no central accumulator blending multiple lights' contributions together. A real multi-light accumulation system is a much bigger tool than this. UniformTint vs PerPixel — see the Influence header's tooltip for the tradeoff.
